situations.intro: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2.5 m/s² for 6 s. It then moves at constant speed for 10 s, and finally brakes uniformly to a stop in 5 s.

questions.text: What is the maximum speed of the car?
What total distance does the car travel?
While the car is braking, its acceleration vector points
choices: opposite to the direction of motion.
questions.solution: The car is slowing down, so a points opposite to v.

situations.intro: A soccer ball is kicked from level ground with an initial speed of 18 m/s at 40° above the horizontal. Ignore air resistance.

questions.text: How long is the ball in the air?
How far from the kicker does the ball land?
What is the speed of the ball at the top of its path?
questions.solution: At the top only vᵧ is zero, so v = vₓ = v₀cosθ = 13.8 m/s.

situations.intro: A stone is thrown horizontally at 8 m/s from the top of a 25 m tall cliff.

questions.text: How far from the base of the cliff does the stone land?
If the stone were thrown horizontally at 16 m/s instead, the time it takes to reach the ground would
questions.solution: The vertical motion does not depend on the horizontal speed.

situations.intro: A river 80 m wide flows east at 1.5 m/s. A boat moves at 4 m/s relative to the water.

questions.text: The boat points due north. How far downstream does it land?
questions.solution: t = W / v_boat = 20 s, drift = v_water · t = 30 m.

questions.text: At what angle west of north must the boat point to land directly across?
Compared with pointing due north, the crossing time when the boat lands directly across is
questions.solution: Only the component v_boat cos θ carries the boat across, so the crossing takes longer.

situations.intro: A 4 kg block sits on a frictionless incline at 30°. It is tied by a light string over a frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a 3 kg block hanging vertically. The blocks are released from rest.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the blocks?
What is the tension in the string?
Compared with the weight of the hanging block, the tension is
questions.solution: The hanging block accelerates downward, so the net force on it points down: T < m₂g.

situations.intro: A 12 kg box is dragged across a level floor at constant velocity by a rope pulling at 25° above the horizontal. The coefficients of friction are μₛ = 0.5 and μₖ = 0.35.

questions.text: What is the tension in the rope?
questions.solution: T cos25° = μₖ(mg − T sin25°), so T = μₖmg/(cos25° + μₖ sin25°) = 39.1 N.

questions.text: The normal force on the box is
questions.solution: The rope pulls partly upward, so the floor pushes up less: N = mg − T sin25°.

situations.intro: A 400 kg roller-coaster car travels upside down at the top of a vertical loop of radius 12 m with a speed of 14 m/s. The car rides on the inside of the track.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the normal force from the track on the car at the top?
What is the minimum speed at the top for the car to stay in contact with the track?
questions.solution: Contact is lost when N = 0: v = √(gr) = 10.8 m/s.

situations.intro: A satellite moves in a circular orbit 2000 km above Earth's surface. (R_E = 6.37 × 10⁶ m, M_E = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²)

questions.text: What is the orbital speed of the satellite?
What is the period of the orbit?
If the satellite had twice the mass, its orbital speed at the same radius would be

situations.intro: A ball is thrown straight up at 15 m/s from a point 2 m above the ground. Ignore air resistance.

questions.text: What is the maximum height of the ball above the ground?
How long after it is thrown does the ball hit the ground?
At the top of its path, the acceleration of the ball is
questions.solution: Gravity acts the whole time. Only the velocity is zero at the top.

situations.intro: A car waits at a red light. The instant the light turns green, the car accelerates at 3 m/s², and at that same instant a truck passes it moving at a constant 20 m/s.

questions.text: How long does it take the car to catch the truck?
questions.solution: ½at² = v_T t, so t = 2v_T/a = 13.3 s.

questions.text: How fast is the car moving when it catches the truck?
questions.solution: v = at = (3)(13.3) = 40 m/s, twice the truck's speed.

questions.text: At the instant the car is moving as fast as the truck, the car is
questions.solution: Until then the truck has been faster, so the gap has been growing. The car is still behind.

situations.intro: A ball is launched from the roof of a 30 m tall building at 12 m/s, 30° above the horizontal. Ignore air resistance.

questions.text: How far from the base of the building does the ball land?
How fast is the ball moving just before it lands?
If the ball were launched at 30° below the horizontal with the same speed, its speed just before landing would be
questions.solution: v = √(v₀² + 2gh) depends only on the speed and height, not the direction.

situations.intro: An airplane flies at 250 km/h relative to the air. A wind blows toward the east at 60 km/h.

questions.text: The pilot points the plane due north. What is its speed relative to the ground?
To travel due north relative to the ground, the pilot should point the plane at what angle west of north?

situations.intro: A 70 kg student stands on a bathroom scale in an elevator.

questions.text: The elevator accelerates upward at 1.8 m/s². What does the scale read?
Later the elevator is moving downward and slowing down. The scale reading is
questions.solution: Slowing while moving down means the acceleration points up, so N > mg.

situations.intro: A horizontal force of 36 N pushes a 5 kg block, which pushes a 7 kg block in front of it across a frictionless floor.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the force the 5 kg block exerts on the 7 kg block?
questions.solution: a = F/(m₁ + m₂) = 3 m/s²; the front block needs F = (7)(3) = 21 N.

questions.text: If the same force pushed on the 7 kg block instead, the contact force between the blocks would be
questions.solution: Now the contact force only accelerates the 5 kg block: (5)(3) = 15 N.

situations.intro: A 3 kg block slides down an incline at 35°. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.25.

questions.text: What is the acceleration of the block?
If the block were instead sliding up the incline, the magnitude of its acceleration would be
questions.solution: Going up, gravity and friction both point down the slope: a = g(sinθ + μₖcosθ).

situations.intro: A car rounds a flat (unbanked) curve of radius 50 m. The coefficient of static friction between the tires and the road is 0.6.

questions.text: What is the maximum speed at which the car can round the curve?
A heavier car on the same curve would have a maximum speed that is
questions.solution: The mass cancels in μₛmg = mv²/r.

situations.intro: A planet has half the radius of Earth and one eighth of Earth's mass. An astronaut weighs 600 N on Earth.

questions.text: What does the astronaut weigh on the planet?

situations.intro: A 5 kg crate starts from rest and is pushed 8 m across a level floor by a 40 N force directed 20° below the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3.

questions.text: How much work does the pushing force do on the crate?
What is the speed of the crate after it has moved 8 m?
questions.solution: N = mg + F sin20° = 62.7 N, friction does −151 J. W_net = 150 J = ½mv², v = 7.75 m/s.

questions.text: How much work does the normal force do on the crate?
questions.solution: The normal force is perpendicular to the displacement.

situations.intro: A toy launcher has a spring with k = 800 N/m. It is compressed 0.15 m and fires a 0.2 kg ball straight up. Treat the launch point as the release point and ignore air resistance.

questions.text: What is the launch speed of the ball?
How high above the launch point does the ball rise?
If the spring were compressed twice as far, the maximum height would be multiplied by
questions.solution: Spring energy ∝ x², so the height is 4 times larger.

situations.intro: A 2 kg ball on a 1.5 m string is pulled aside until the string makes 60° with the vertical, then released from rest.

questions.text: What is the speed of the ball at the lowest point?
What is the tension in the string at the lowest point?

situations.intro: A 1200 kg car accelerates from rest to 25 m/s in 9 s on a level road. Ignore friction and air resistance.

questions.text: What average power does the engine deliver?
To reach 50 m/s from rest in the same time, the average power would need to be multiplied by
questions.solution: K ∝ v², so doubling the final speed takes 4 times the energy in the same time.

situations.intro: A 1500 kg car moving east at 20 m/s rear-ends a 2500 kg truck at rest. The two vehicles lock together.

questions.text: What is their speed just after the collision?
How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision?
questions.solution: K before = 300 kJ, after = ½(4000)(7.5²) = 112.5 kJ, lost 188 kJ.

questions.text: During the collision, the force of the truck on the car is
choices: larger than the force of the car on the truck.
equal in size to the force of the car on the truck.
smaller than the force of the car on the truck.
questions.solution: Newton's third law: the forces are equal and opposite.

situations.intro: A 0.5 kg ball moving at 4 m/s makes a head-on elastic collision with a 1.5 kg ball at rest.

questions.text: What is the velocity of the 0.5 kg ball after the collision?
questions.solution: v₁′ = (m₁ − m₂)/(m₁ + m₂) · v = (−1/2)(4) = -2 m/s, so 2.0 m/s backward.

questions.text: What is the speed of the 1.5 kg ball after the collision?

situations.intro: A 0.15 kg baseball arrives at a bat at 35 m/s and leaves in the opposite direction at 45 m/s. The ball is in contact with the bat for 1.2 ms.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the average force of the bat on the ball?
The impulse on the ball points
choices: in the direction of the ball's final velocity.
in the direction of the ball's initial velocity.
questions.solution: Δp = p_f − p_i points along the final velocity here.

situations.intro: A ceiling fan starts from rest and speeds up uniformly to 900 rpm in 6.0 s. Its blades are 0.40 m long.

questions.text: What is the angular acceleration of the fan?
How many revolutions does the fan make during these 6.0 s?
Compared with the blade tip, a point halfway along the blade has
choices: the same angular speed and half the linear speed.
half the angular speed and the same linear speed.
the same angular speed and the same linear speed.
questions.solution: Every point on a rigid body shares ω, and v = ωr.

situations.intro: A 2.0 kg uniform rod 1.2 m long has a 0.50 kg point mass attached at each end.

questions.text: What is the moment of inertia about an axis through the center of the rod, perpendicular to it?

situations.intro: A 4 kg block is released from rest at the top of a ramp 3 m high. On the way down, friction does −40 J of work on it.

questions.text: What is the speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp?
The change in the mechanical energy of the block is
questions.solution: Non-conservative work changes mechanical energy: ΔE = W_friction = −40 J.

situations.intro: A 2 kg block slides at 3 m/s across a frictionless floor and runs into a spring with k = 450 N/m.

questions.text: What is the maximum compression of the spring?
What is the speed of the block when the spring is compressed 0.10 m?
The magnitude of the block's acceleration is largest
choices: at the moment it first touches the spring.
questions.solution: The spring force kx is largest when x is largest.

situations.intro: A force acts on a 3.0 kg cart along the x axis. It rises linearly from 0 at x = 0 to 30 N at x = 4.0 m, then stays at 30 N until x = 6.0 m. The cart starts from rest on a frictionless track.

questions.text: How much work does the force do from x = 0 to x = 6.0 m?
What is the speed of the cart at x = 6.0 m?

situations.intro: A 60 kg skier leaves the top of a 40 m high frictionless hill moving at 5.0 m/s.

questions.text: What is the skier's speed at the bottom?
A heavier skier starting the same way would reach the bottom with a speed that is
questions.solution: The mass cancels in the energy equation.

situations.intro: An 80 kg astronaut floating at rest outside a space station throws a 4.0 kg wrench at 6.0 m/s.

questions.text: What is the astronaut's recoil speed?
After the throw, the kinetic energy of the wrench is
questions.solution: Equal momenta: K = p²/2m, so the smaller mass has more kinetic energy.

situations.intro: A 1000 kg car moving east at 15 m/s collides at an intersection with a 1500 kg car moving north at 10 m/s. The cars stick together.

questions.text: What is the speed of the wreck just after the collision?
In what direction does the wreck move just after the collision?
questions.solution: pᵧ = pₓ, so the angle is 45° north of east.

situations.intro: Three small objects lie on the x axis: 2.0 kg at x = 0, 3.0 kg at x = 2.0 m and 5.0 kg at x = 4.0 m.

questions.text: Where is the center of mass?
The objects sit on frictionless ice and push each other apart. The center of mass
questions.solution: Internal forces cannot move the center of mass of an isolated system.

situations.intro: A 0.020 kg bullet is fired into a 2.0 kg wooden block hanging from a long string. The bullet embeds in the block, and the block swings up 0.12 m.

questions.text: What was the bullet's speed just before impact?
During the very short collision itself, which quantity is conserved?
questions.solution: The collision is perfectly inelastic: momentum is conserved, kinetic energy is not.

situations.intro: A car moves at 72 km/h. Its tires have a radius of 0.35 m and roll without slipping.

questions.text: What is the angular speed of the tires?

situations.intro: A solid disk of mass 8.0 kg and radius 0.30 m spins at 120 rpm about its central axis.

questions.text: What is its rotational kinetic energy?
questions.solution: I = ½MR² = 0.36 kg·m², ω = 12.6 rad/s, K = ½Iω² = 28.4 J.

questions.text: A thin ring with the same mass and radius spinning at the same rate has a kinetic energy that is
questions.solution: I_ring = MR² is twice I_disk = ½MR².

situations.intro: A mechanic pulls on the end of a 0.25 m wrench with an 80 N force directed at 60° to the wrench handle.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the torque on the bolt?

situations.intro: A 1.0 kg block hangs from a light rope wrapped around a pulley that is a uniform solid disk (M = 2.0 kg, R = 0.10 m). The pulley turns without friction, and the block is released from rest.

questions.text: What is the acceleration of the block?
questions.solution: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) → a = mg/(m + M/2) = 4.91 m/s².

questions.text: What is the tension in the rope?
If the pulley were a thin ring with the same mass and radius, the block's acceleration would be
questions.solution: A ring has a larger moment of inertia, so it resists turning more.

situations.intro: A solid sphere (m = 2.0 kg, R = 0.10 m) rolls without slipping from rest down an incline. It descends a vertical height of 1.5 m.

questions.text: What is the speed of the sphere at the bottom?
What fraction of the sphere's kinetic energy at the bottom is rotational?
How much work does static friction do on the sphere while it rolls?
questions.solution: The contact point is momentarily at rest, so static friction does no work.

situations.intro: A uniform 6.0 m plank of mass 30 kg rests on supports at its two ends. A 70 kg person stands 1.5 m from the left end.

questions.text: What upward force does the right support exert?
questions.solution: Torques about the left end: R(6) = (30g)(3) + (70g)(1.5), R = 319 N.

questions.text: What upward force does the left support exert?
As the person walks toward the right end, the force from the left support
questions.solution: More of the weight shifts onto the right support.

situations.intro: A figure skater spins at 2.0 rev/s with her arms out (I = 4.0 kg·m²). She pulls her arms in, reducing her moment of inertia to 1.6 kg·m².

questions.text: What is her new rate of spin?
Her rotational kinetic energy
questions.solution: K = L²/2I. L is fixed and I drops, so K rises. Her muscles do the work.

situations.intro: A 30 kg child runs at 4.0 m/s along a line tangent to the edge of a merry-go-round and jumps on at its edge. The merry-go-round is a uniform disk of mass 120 kg and radius 2.0 m, initially at rest.

questions.text: What is the angular speed of the merry-go-round just after the child lands?
Compared with before the jump, the total kinetic energy afterward is
questions.solution: This is an inelastic "collision": L is conserved but kinetic energy is not.

situations.intro: A constant torque of 6.0 N·m acts on a wheel (I = 1.5 kg·m²) that starts at rest.

questions.text: What is the angular momentum of the wheel after 4.0 s?

situations.intro: A 0.80 kg block on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring with k = 200 N/m. It oscillates with an amplitude of 0.10 m.

questions.text: What is the period of the oscillation?
What is the maximum speed of the block?
When the block is at x = A/2, its speed is what fraction of v_max?

situations.intro: A simple pendulum has a period of 2.0 s on Earth. It is taken to a planet where g is one quarter of its value on Earth.

questions.text: What is its period on the planet?
questions.solution: T ∝ 1/√g; g/4 doubles the period to 4.0 s.

questions.text: If the amplitude of the swing were doubled (still small), the period would
questions.solution: For small oscillations the period does not depend on amplitude.

situations.intro: A door is 1.0 m wide. You push with a 40 N force at a point 0.50 m from the hinges, at 45° to the door.

questions.text: What torque do you exert about the hinges?

situations.intro: An Atwood machine has masses of 3.0 kg and 5.0 kg on either side of a pulley that is a uniform solid disk (M = 4.0 kg, R = 0.15 m). The rope does not slip and the axle is frictionless.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the masses?
What is the tension in the rope on the 3.0 kg side?
How do the tensions on the two sides compare?
choices: The tension on the 3.0 kg side is larger.
The tension on the 5.0 kg side is larger.
questions.solution: A net torque is needed to give the massive pulley its angular acceleration, so T₂ > T₁.

situations.intro: A thin hoop and a solid cylinder, with the same mass and radius, are released together from rest at the top of the same incline and roll without slipping. The top is 2.0 m above the bottom.

questions.text: Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.solution: The cylinder has a smaller I/MR², so less of its energy goes into rotation.

questions.text: What is the speed of the hoop at the bottom?
questions.solution: mgh = ½mv² + ½(mR²)(v/R)² = mv² → v = √(gh) = 4.43 m/s.

situations.intro: A grinding wheel is a uniform disk of mass 5.0 kg and radius 0.20 m, spinning at 300 rad/s. A tool is pressed against its rim with a normal force of 40 N, and the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.60.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the angular acceleration of the wheel?
How long does the wheel take to stop?

situations.intro: A uniform horizontal beam 4.0 m long with a mass of 20 kg is hinged to a wall at one end. A cable attached to the other end makes a 30° angle with the beam. A 50 kg sign hangs from the end of the beam.

questions.text: What is the tension in the cable?
questions.solution: Torques about the hinge: T sin30°(4) = (20g)(2) + (50g)(4), T = 1180 N.

questions.text: What is the horizontal force the hinge exerts on the beam?
If the cable were attached to the wall higher up, so it made a larger angle with the beam, the tension would
questions.solution: A larger angle gives a larger perpendicular component, so less tension is needed for the same torque.

situations.intro: Disk A (I = 0.50 kg·m²) spins at 30 rad/s. Disk B (I = 1.0 kg·m²), initially not spinning, is dropped onto it along the same axle, and the disks stick together.

questions.text: What is the final angular speed?
What fraction of the initial kinetic energy is lost?
questions.solution: K_f/K_i = I_A/(I_A + I_B) = 1/3, so 2/3 is lost.

situations.intro: A 2.0 kg ball moves at a constant 5.0 m/s in the +x direction along the line y = 3.0 m.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of the ball's angular momentum about the origin?
As the ball moves along the line, its angular momentum about the origin
questions.solution: No force acts, so no torque acts, and the perpendicular distance stays 3.0 m.

situations.intro: A 0.50 kg block on a spring moves according to x(t) = (0.12 m) cos(8.0t), with t in seconds.

questions.text: What is the spring constant?
What is the total mechanical energy of the oscillation?
If the mass were four times larger (same spring), the period would

situations.intro: A 0.30 kg mass hangs at rest from a vertical spring, which it stretches by 6.0 cm.

questions.text: If the mass is pulled down slightly and released, what is the period of oscillation?

situations.intro: You want to build a simple pendulum with a period of 1.5 s on Earth.

questions.text: How long should the pendulum be?
